_readme: IMP-11. Exceptions to check-dead-machinery.mjs, each with a reason someone
can evaluate later. This is a record of decisions, not a mute button.
A reason beginning with 'KNOWN GAP' means the thing genuinely is not wired
up yet. Those are counted and reported separately on every run, so unfinished
work stays visible in the check's own output instead of being silenced by
being written down. Clear them by wiring the thing up, not by editing the
The gap count jumped on 2026-07-31. It was not a new outbreak: rule 1 was
counting TypeScript COMMENTS as callers and rule 3 could not fire at all.
Everything added that day was already in this state and invisible, and each
entry was checked against the live database before being written down.
A fourth group, function_overloads, was added on 2026-07-31. Postgres
identifies a function by name AND argument types, so one name can be two
functions — skip_visit was, for a month, and rule 1 could not see the dead
one because the live one had callers. An entry here means an overload set is
deliberate and says which signatures are meant. There are none today.

endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/announcement: Deliberately unscheduled, and no longer unreachable. The 120-line send moved to lib/announcement-emails.server, which a platform admin now invokes per announcement from /platform/announcements — so an announcement marked send_email actually gets sent, which it never did before. This endpoint stays as the shape a scheduler needs if the owner ever wants one; scheduling platform-wide outbound email is their decision, not a cleanup task. Both callers share a per-recipient idempotency key, so adding a cron later cannot double-send.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/platform-str: Stripe platform webhook endpoint, for HoundStack's own SaaS billing (bucket A).
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/qbo-callback: QuickBooks OAuth redirect target — the browser lands here after a tenant authorizes.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/stripe.ts: Stripe Connect webhook endpoint. Called by Stripe on tenant payment events.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/weekly-diges: pg_cron job 'weekly-digest', 0 13 * * 1 — created by 20260731130000, verified in cron.job.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/leads.ts: Public lead-capture form, embedded on tenant websites. Called by a browser from outside the app.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/verify-email.ts: Target of the verification link in a signup email.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/email/auth/webhook.ts: Supabase Auth send-email hook — Supabase calls this to render auth mail.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/email/suppression.ts: Provider bounce/complaint webhook — writes the suppression list.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/email/transactional/send.ts: NO CALLER, and the previous reason here was wrong: it claimed the app's own notification code calls this server-to-server. It does not. Nothing in src/ references the path, and lib/email/enqueue.server.ts says outright that system code 'bypasses /email/transactional/send auth by writing directly to the pgmq queue'. The endpoint also requires a user Bearer JWT, which system code has none of. Kept because it is a reachable authenticated endpoint a future user-initiated send could use; the exemption now records that it is unused rather than pretending it is wired.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/email/unsubscribe.ts: Target of the List-Unsubscribe header and the footer link in every marketing email.

uncalled_rpcs.is_visit_tech: Called from ~10 SQL bodies in this tree and from the storage policy in 20260701161658. The previous reason claimed the scanner could not see it because bootstrap-dump policies are not files — but that policy IS a file, so the stated premise was false even though the exemption is harmless. Kept as a no-op guard against the scanner's SQL-body parsing regressing.
